rules.title: Error grouping rules
rules.description: Tried in order on the errors seen from now on; the first that matches holds. It merges them into one group per service, or keeps them out of groups (their requests still count as failed). A saved rule applies on every node within half a minute.

fields.name: Name
fields.name_hint: A merged group is named by it.

rules.patterns_hint: Each matches the whole text, ignoring case, with * for any text; an empty one matches anything. Fill in at least one.
rules.preview_one: {{count}} listed error group fits this rule. Groups already made stay as they are: the rule applies to errors seen from now on.
rules.preview_other: {{count}} listed error groups fit this rule. Groups already made stay as they are: the rule applies to errors seen from now on.
rules.remove_description: Errors seen from now on are no longer grouped by it; the groups it made stay.

runtime.none_title: No runtime metrics from this service
runtime.none_description: Charts appear by language once the service sends runtime metrics with its service.name: the process, and the runtime of JVM, Go, Node.js, .NET, Python, Ruby, PHP, Rust (Tokio) and Erlang / Elixir. OpenTelemetry's conventions and the common Prometheus client of each language are both read.

profile.title: Profiling
profile.description: The service's profiles of the range merged into a flame graph, one type at a time
profile.none: No profile from this service in this range
profile.none_description: Once continuous profiling is set up, flame graphs of CPU, wall clock, allocations, heap, locks and more show here.
profile.empty: No sample of this type in this range

naming.traces_keep: Traces keep the names spans carry
naming.unread: A pattern cannot be read here; the server reads Rust regular expressions and says when it cannot either.

environments.title: Environment mapping
environments.hint: An environment named one way is read as another, case aside, as spans are read
environments.empty: No mapping: environments are read as named.

aliases.title: Service aliases
aliases.hint: What an alias reported is read as its service on every APM page, data already kept included; taking the alias away reads them apart again

issues.itself: A service is not its own alias.

issues.chained: An alias leads to a service that is itself an alias.
